parsed.rationale: Both `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` (Shared/Playback/Sources/MP3Streamer/Playback/AudioEnginePlayerProtocol.swift:34) and `TimeShiftablePlayer` (Shared/Playback/Sources/PlaybackCore/Protocols/TimeShiftablePlayer.swift:20) share the members `installRenderTap:()`, `removeRenderTap:()`, `isPlaying:Bool`, and `stop:()`, which represent a minimal common behavioral contract for any audio player in the `Playback` package. Extracting these four members into a new `AudioPlayerCore` base protocol — housed in a shared location within the `Playback` package (e.g., `Shared/Playback/Sources/PlaybackCore/Protocols/AudioPlayerCore.swift`) — removes the implicit duplication without conflating the two protocols' distinct responsibilities: `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` remains a low-level engine contract (buffer scheduling, volume, render-tap streams) while `TimeShiftablePlayer` remains a high-level time-shifting contract. Both child protocols would declare conformance to `AudioPlayerCore`, making the shared surface explicit and enabling code that only needs basic playback control to depend on the narrower type. Neither record carries any restraint markers (`is_test`, `is_mock`, `is_sample_app`, `is_codegen` are all false), so the refactor is safe.
